title: Betrayers of Kamigawa: card flavor text

paragraphs.text: "Rise like the sun, stand like the mountain, charge like the lion, die as a hero." —General Takeno
"Crease the folds, bend the paper, turn the spirits, shield the soul."
"The clashing warriors turned to face O-Kagachi, the greatest kami, and their sigh of awe was their last breath." —*Great Battles of Kamigawa*
"There is a shining in the mortal heart that even the kami cannot reach." —Sensei Golden-Tail
"Forgive me, Saburo. I could not save you. But your blade will not rest in my hand."
"Across the rift of battle, a bridge of gossamer. And for one moment, it holds." —Snow-Fur, kitsune poet
It remembered all the shadows lantern-cast upon its paper wings, and sometimes those silhouettes played across its shape again, acting out silent tragedies.
"The bonds of bushido will draw the dishonored back someday, and I will be there waiting."
"Who am I to judge who is deserving and who is not? That is a question for lords, not healers."
"I can staunch their blood, mend their flesh, and knit their bones. But I cannot restore their hope." —Tender-Hand, kitsune healer
Her angry call split the sky. From that rift descended her champions.
"I wish there were no use for those with my talents. I wish that I could walk Kamigawa forgotten and unneeded, with no war wounds to heal and no broken bones to mend."
At night he perfected his aim, shooting spiderwebs by starlight.
Isolated on its little candlewick, the kami never heard of the crime that drove its comrades to war.
"The jeweler, the potter, the smith . . . They all imbue a bit of their souls into their creations. The kami destroy that crafted mortal shell and absorb the soul within." —Noboru, master kitemaker
It was as though the sky opened its eyes and found what it saw displeasing.
Reluctant to strike at the kami directly, some kitsune trained in more passive fighting techniques.
"As I died, I rejoiced. I would see my family again. But then I woke up back on the battlefield. Back in Kamigawa. Back in hell." —Kenzo the Hardhearted
"Such a small thing, a drop of water . . . And yet enough of them together can flood a field, cleanse a mire, or choke a forest."
"Once, I looked to the mists for wisdom. Now I wish only for understanding."
The bolt struck with a flash and there was a terrible sound, as of glass shattering, but the creature was unharmed.
When it's finished, all that's left of you is a ripple on a still pond.
Each spell is an intricate tapestry, and Kira is the great unraveler.
Woven from threads of the spirit world, the mistcloak rendered its wearer invisible, but quickly fell to tatters.
Like storm water through the segments of bamboo, the spell followed the links of magic. Then it destroyed them.
Many kami could fly, which put some warriors at a distinct disadvantage. The mages of Minamo took it upon themselves to correct that imbalance.
"This world is a dream. We cling to our toys like children, but sooner or later we must learn to live without them." —Sensei Hisoka
"If wisdom is a river, then we cup our hands, reach in, and drink from it in sips. The kami, however, are like fish, swimming, breathing, surrounded in its presence." —Dosan the Falling Leaf
A child's whisper could crack its shell, but not even an oni's scream could penetrate it.
"All things return to their beginnings. The waters that spill across the Kamitaki Falls flow to sea, only to be returned to her as the rain that joins the mighty river." —Dosan the Falling Leaf
"Do not fall into the trap of thinking you understand the kami. Cannot a drop of water be dew on the meadow, a glacier's thaw, or the tear of a child?" —Sensei Hisoka
"Over time, Konda grew ever more suspicious, fearing even his most loyal allies were being manipulated by unseen hands." —*The History of Kamigawa*
"The war sent Kamigawa into turmoil. Here it was spring and there winter. For some, time stood still, while for others, moments flashed past like minnows in a pond." —*Observations of the Kami War*
"The two youths argued and tempers flared. One youth opened his mouth to utter a vile curse, but what he spat out instead was a kami of poison and filth." —Sensei Golden-Tail

"What will it say on our graves, Lord Konda? Will it say we led our world to conquer immortal forces or that we were crushed by our own arrogance? At each defeat, I wonder." —Sensei Hisoka, letter to Lord Konda
"Kyoki, Eater of Minds, Corrupter of Thoughts, Bringer of Madness, Lord of Fear. Return, by our blood, and walk again." —Ogre chant
"As more oni walked Kamigawa, more darkness infested its inhabitants' souls." —*The History of Kamigawa*
"The Okiba Gang! Night-cursed thieves and assassins! I've had enough of their meddling! Triple the guard!" —Marrow-Gnawer
Once freed, the oni demanded more and more sacrifices to appease them. The ogres happily obliged.
"The wizards of Takenuma Swamp faced the horrors of humanity every day. It's no wonder they fared so well against the kami." —*Observations of the Kami War*
"Where a once-proud human city stood, only the ruins of Numai remain, deep amid rotting bamboo and plagued by oni." —*The History of Kamigawa*
"Your lungs may not draw breath, but while your hands can grip a sword, you will be useful to me." —Nighteyes, nezumi necromancer
"I prefer to weave my magic through oni blood, but yours will do in a pinch."

"As the kami passed over the village of Mita, the inhabitants relived their three most grievous tragedies. Some cried. Some raged. Some were driven to madness. But the next morning, none possessed the will to fight." —*Observations of the Kami War*

It took ninety-nine monks to weave the spell that trapped Yukora. Upon the death of the ninety-nine, the spell was broken, and the demon returned to the mortal world seeking vengeance for its imprisonment.
"It remains unclear whether the akki shamans could in fact create storms or simply predicted them." —*The History of Kamigawa*
Akki were very territorial, attacking and destroying any settlements that came too close to their mountain homes. The more successful their raids, the bolder they became.
There was a dull thunder at the vanguard, then shocked cries in the midst of the column. Moments later, Takada, last of the rearguard, faced the kami alone.
"As the war progressed, the destruction the kami caused became more widespread and less predictable." —*Observations of the Kami War*
"We searched their bodies for signs of the blades that had killed them, but found nothing more than scorched flesh." —Tender-Hand, kitsune healer
Many ogres extracted blood oaths from the oni they summoned. Others simply extracted blood.
Mountain ogres allowed blizzards to sheathe them in ice, both to reinforce their armor and to hide their pungent musk from potential prey.
Its bite will take off more than a toe.
Akki shells provided good protection when downhill charging became headlong tumbling.
Hidetsugu held over a dozen oni in blood oath. At his touch, rocks scorched. At his word, cities burned.

"In desperation, Konda sent warriors to parley with the ogre-magi. No one knows whether they were slaughtered at Shinka or if they even reached its bloodstained walls." —*Observations of the Kami War*

"Thunder broke the brittle silence over the Araba. A surge of raw energy lifted the soldier's body into the air and briefly, in the heart of the flash, he saw the face of a god." —*Great Battles of Kamigawa*
"Here fell Ishi-Ishi, King of the Flaming Pebbles, Scourge of the Mountain Kami, Lover of Goats. May his shell never burn." —Cave inscription

"Early in his reign, Konda fell ill. His head burned with fever, and he saw visions of his future. In them, he saw a spirit-child, and, in that child's eyes, a way to make his empire last forever." —*The History of Kamigawa*
"Those ogres who did not embrace oni worship were cast out, cursed, and forced into hermitage, waiting for the day the oni would come for them." —*The History of Kamigawa*
"Understanding is not a virtue of the ogre. Do not seek to reason your way into Shinka Keep." —Kiku, Night's Flower
"The soratami scoff at the perils of Jukai, calling the forest an 'unruly garden.' Perhaps we should send them a rose such as this." —Dokai, Weaver of Life
"The race is run in the mind before the first step is taken." —Dosan the Falling Leaf
"On the fifty-seventh day of the Battle of Silk, the bell again tolled in hopes of summoning mortal aid. This time, a new breed of kami rose to answer its call." —*Great Battles of Kamigawa*
"I do not care if he claims no allegiance in this war. Find him, Takeno." —Lord Konda
"Walk the world and you'll find your soul; search your soul and you'll discover the world." —Diary of Azusa
"The husk splits like a madman's smile And mystery steps forth." —Snow-Fur, kitsune poet
"You know its mood by the plants that spring up around it. When it is placid, fields of lilies flow in its wake; when it is angry, every stem has a thorn." —Isao, Enlightened Bushi
"Say, what rhymes with 'run for your lives'?" —Ku-Ku, akki poet
"That energy was once granted to growing things. Now the kami keep it for themselves, releasing it in sudden floods that overwhelm flesh and foliage alike." —Sakiko, Mother of Summer
"We arrived at the battlefield too late. *Again*. Another error on your part, and you will have to answer to me personally." —General Takeno, letter to the imperial mapmaker
Only in mirrors do heroes find their equal.
"Behind the eyelids, a flickering flame. Beneath the dream, a flickering sorrow. Can peace find you in this sleep When all the world is tossed by war?" —Snow-Fur, kitsune poet
Masako was privy to a great many of Konda's deepest secrets, and her hair was always perfect.
"One scratch on a wall meant safe passage, two that the target had already been raided, and three warned of a trap." —*Weaponry of Kamigawa*
"This god held prisoner in human hands has put all humanity in the hands of angry gods." —Masako the Humorless
Listen at its walls and you will hear the whispers of gods.
paragraphs.card: Gods' Eye, Gate to the Reikai
